To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

barley supplementation of the diet decreased the polysaccharide degrading activity of the solid associated bacteria, without modifying the proportion of the three celluloytic bacterial species attached to plant particles.
the addition of cereal grains to a hay-based diet decreased the fibrolytase activities of the solid-associated rumen bacteria and the in situ degradation rate of the hay.
the negative effect of barley supplementation on the ruminal degradation rate of hay was due to a decrease of the fibrolysis activity of the solid-associated bacterial population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of barley supplementation on the ruminal fibrolytic and cellulolytic bacterial activities, and their relationships to the ruminal digestion of forage in cows.
the effect of a dietary change (barley supplementation) on the structure of the fibrolytical community and the cellulolytic activity of the ruminal solid-associated bacteria.
the effects of cereal supplementation on the ruminal fibrolytic bacterial community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cellulolytic community is not the main target of the negative effect of cereal supplementation.
the structure of the rumen cellulolytic bacterial communities is more complex and more stable than the fibrolytically active bacteria.
cereal supplementation modified the cellulolytic activity but not cellulolytic community structure associated with rumen particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
barley supplementation modified the structure of the fibrolytically-active SAB community, but not the structure and the proportion of the cellulolytically-active SABC community.
cereal supplementation modified the fibolytic activity but not structure of the cellulolitic bacterial community associated with solid digesta.
cereal supplementation modified the fibolytic activity but not cellulolytic community structure of the solid-associated bacterial community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ruminal bacterial community is not the main factor involved in the rumen degradation of forage.

barley supplementation did not modify either the structure of the ruminal cellulolytic bacterial population or the cellulolytic activities of the S. albus, F. succinogenes and R. flavefaciens species.
the cellulolytic bacteria are present on the plant particles and that the structure of the bacterial cellulolytic community is not modified by barley supplementation.
